gap: None of the results ChatGPT got says that a 2-PC, 1-monitor KVM rated '4K 60 Hz' tops out at 497.7 million pixels per second. A 1440p 144 Hz monitor needs 530.8 Mpx/s (6.7% more), so the $54.99 UGREEN and the $129.99 TESmart HKS201-P23 that ChatGPT recommended cap a 1440p monitor at 120 Hz. TESmart's cheapest 2-PC, 1-monitor model that lists 1440p above 120 Hz is the HKS201-M24 at $269.
standout_why: I opened the two pages ChatGPT cited. DeskDNA (best-kvm-switch) lists the UGREEN's modes (4K@60, 1440p@120, 1080p@240) and says 'HDMI covers 4K@60Hz / 1080p@240Hz' and 'DisplayPort 1.4 is required for 4K@144Hz'. It never says that 4K60 does not mean 1440p 144 Hz, and it gives no pixel-rate or bandwidth math. iTechGuides gives no Gbps figure for any video mode and never mentions 1440p 144 Hz. Neither page explains that the mode lists come from one fixed pixel-rate ceiling, and neither puts a price on going past it.
decides: This splits ChatGPT's pick by monitor. For 4K60, 3440×1440 at 100 Hz or 1080p at 240 Hz, the cheap HDMI 2.0 switch is enough and the UGREEN/TESmart HKS201-P23 recommendation holds. For a 1440p 144/165 Hz gaming monitor, which is the most common upgrade, those switches hold it to 120 Hz. The right pick becomes the TESmart HKS201-M24 ($269, lists 2560×1440@240 Hz and 3440×1440@144 Hz). That costs $139.01 more than the HKS201-P23, still well under ChatGPT's $449.85 StarTech. ChatGPT's own follow-up question about the monitor's refresh rate is where this number belongs.
